{{Short description|Disproved conjecture}}
[[File:Block scheme of control system.jpg|thumb|
Fig. 1. Block scheme of control system.  ''G''(''s'') – linear [[transfer function]], ''f''(''e'') – single-valued, continuous, differentiable function]]

'''Kalman's conjecture''' or '''Kalman problem''' is a disproved [[conjecture]] on absolute stability of 
[[nonlinear control]] system  with one scalar nonlinearity, which belongs to the sector of [[linear stability]].  Kalman's conjecture is a strengthening of [[Aizerman's conjecture]]
and is a special case of [[Markus–Yamabe conjecture]].  This conjecture was proven false but led to the (valid) [[Nonlinear control#Absolute stability problem|sufficient criteria on absolute stability]].

== Mathematical statement of Kalman's conjecture (Kalman problem)==
In 1957 [[R. E. Kalman]] in his paper
<ref name=1957-Kalman>{{cite journal
 | author = Kalman R.E. 
 | year = 1957
 | title = Physical and Mathematical mechanisms of instability in nonlinear automatic control systems 
 | journal = Transactions of ASME
 | volume = 79
 | number = 3
 | pages = 553&ndash;566
}}
</ref> stated the following:
<blockquote>
If ''f''(''e'') in Fig. 1 is replaced by constants ''K'' corresponding to all possible values of ''f''<nowiki>'</nowiki>(''e''), and it is found that the closed-loop system is stable for all such ''K'', then it intuitively clear that the system must be monostable; i.e., all transient solutions will converge to a unique, stable critical point.
</blockquote>

Kalman's statement can be reformulated in the following conjecture:<ref name=2020-TiSU-Kalman>{{cite journal | 
  author1=Kuznetsov N.V. | 
  year = 2020| 
  title = Theory of hidden oscillations and stability of control systems| 
 journal = Journal of Computer and Systems Sciences International| 
 volume = 59| number = 5|pages = 647&ndash;668| 
 url = https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1134/S1064230720050093.pdf|
 doi = 10.1134/S1064230720050093| 
 s2cid = 225304463}}
</ref>
<blockquote>
Consider a system with one scalar nonlinearity
:<math>  
  \frac{dx}{dt}=Px+qf(e),\quad e=r^*x \quad x\in R^n,
</math>
where ''P'' is a constant ''n''×''n'' matrix, ''q'', ''r'' are constant ''n''-dimensional vectors, ∗ is an operation of transposition, ''f''(''e'') is scalar function, and ''f''(0)&nbsp;=&nbsp;0. Suppose, ''f''(''e'') is a differentiable function and the following condition
:<math>
 k_1 < f'(e)< k_2. \,
</math>
is valid. Then Kalman's conjecture is that the system is stable in the large (i.e. a unique stationary point is a global [[attractor]]) if all linear systems with ''f''(''e'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ke'', ''k''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;(''k''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;''k''<sub>2</sub>) are asymptotically stable.
</blockquote>

In [[Aizerman's conjecture]] in place of the condition on the derivative of nonlinearity it is required that the nonlinearity itself belongs to the linear sector.

Kalman's conjecture is true for ''n''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;3 and for ''n''&nbsp;>&nbsp;3 there are effective methods for construction of counterexamples:<ref>{{cite journal
 |author1=Bragin V.O. |author2=Vagaitsev V.I. |author3=Kuznetsov N.V. |author4=Leonov G.A. | year = 2011
 | title = Algorithms for Finding Hidden Oscillations in Nonlinear Systems. The Aizerman and Kalman Conjectures and Chua's Circuits
 | journal = Journal of Computer and Systems Sciences International
 | volume = 50
 | number = 5
 | pages = 511&ndash;543
 | url = https://www.math.spbu.ru/user/nk/PDF/2011-TiSU-Hidden-oscillations-attractors-Aizerman-Kalman-conjectures.pdf
 | doi = 10.1134/S106423071104006X|s2cid=21657305 }}
</ref><ref name=2011-IJBC-Hidden-attractors>{{cite journal |author1=Leonov G.A. |author2=Kuznetsov N.V. | 
year = 2013 | 
title = Hidden attractors in dynamical systems. From hidden oscillations in Hilbert-Kolmogorov, Aizerman, and Kalman problems to hidden chaotic attractor in Chua circuits | 
journal = International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos | 
volume = 23 | 
issue = 1 | 
pages = 1330002–219|
doi = 10.1142/S0218127413300024|bibcode=2013IJBC...2330002L | 
doi-access =  }}
</ref> the nonlinearity derivative belongs to the sector of linear stability, and a unique stable equilibrium coexists with a stable periodic solution ([[hidden oscillation]]). In discrete-time, the Kalman conjecture is only true for n=1, counterexamples for  ''n''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;2 can be constructed.<ref>{{cite book
 |author1=Carrasco J. |author2=Heath W. P. |author3=de la Sen M. |title=2015 European Control Conference (ECC) |chapter=Second-order counterexample to the discrete-time Kalman conjecture | year = 2015
|pages=981–985 |doi=10.1109/ECC.2015.7330669 |isbn=978-3-9524269-3-7 |s2cid=1600711 }}
</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 |author1=Heath W. P. |author2=Carrasco J |author3=de la Sen M. | year = 2015
 | title = Second-order counterexamples to the discrete-time Kalman conjecture
 | journal = Automatica |volume=60 |pages=140–144 | doi = 10.1016/j.automatica.2015.07.005
|url=https://pure.manchester.ac.uk/ws/files/20961286/POST-PEER-REVIEW-NON-PUBLISHERS.PDF }}
</ref>

The development of Kalman's ideas on global stability based on the stability of [[linear approximation]] for a cylindrical [[phase space]] gave rise to the [[Andrew_Viterbi#Viterbi%27s_problem_on_the_coincidence_of_PLL_ranges|Viterbi problem on the coincidence of phase-locked loop ranges]].<ref name=2025-ND-KuznetsovLKKA>{{cite journal
 | last1=Kuznetsov | first1=N.V.
 | last2=Lobachev | first2=M.Y.
 | last3=Kudryashova | first3=E.V.
 | last4=Kuznetsova | first4=O.A.
 | last5=Arseniev | first5=D.G.
 | title=The Viterbi problem on coincidence of phase-locked loop lock-in, pull-in, and hold-in ranges
 | journal=Nonlinear Dynamics
 | doi=10.1007/s11071-025-11040-3
 | volume= | issue= | pages=
 | year=2025
 | doi-access=free
 }}</ref>
